---
title: "Assignments and Assessment"
---

Assignments are designed as stages of one professional survey workflow. Detailed prompts, rubrics, templates, and submission links will be released on Canvas.

## Assessment map

| Category | Weight | Individual or collaborative? |
|---|---:|---|
| Preparation and professional participation | 10% | Individual |
| R and statistics labs | 25% | Individual, with permitted collaboration |
| Individual methods memos | 15% | Individual |
| Univision project milestones | 25% | Primarily collaborative |
| Coauthored LBJ/Univision report | 20% | Collaborative |
| Reflection and contribution statement | 5% | Individual |

## R and statistics labs · 25%

Five substantial labs integrate R programming, statistical reasoning, and survey analysis:

1. R, Quarto, importing, cleaning, recoding, and documenting survey data.
2. Descriptive statistics, cross-tabulations, measurement, and visualization.
3. Sampling, simulation, margins of error, confidence intervals, and basic hypothesis tests.
4. Survey weights, design effects, and weighted estimation.
5. Regression, predicted probabilities, graphics, and reproducible reporting.

Most lab work will be completed together during class. Each lab concludes with a shorter **On Your Own** section that students complete and submit individually. Labs are graded on statistical reasoning, readable and functioning code, reproducibility, appropriate checks, and clear interpretation.

## Individual methods memos · 15%

Four concise memos ask students to defend methodological decisions:

1. **Poll autopsy:** evaluate what a published poll permits us to conclude.
2. **Measurement memo:** diagnose and revise problematic survey questions.
3. **Sampling and mode memo:** recommend a feasible design and explain its limitations.
4. **Interpretation memo:** write defensible public claims from a set of survey estimates.

## Univision project milestones · 25%

Milestones make the collaborative process visible and accountable.

| Milestone | Deliverable |
|---|---|
| Project charter | Research objectives, audiences, roles, decision rules, and timeline |
| Measurement package | Construct map, proposed module, and design rationale |
| Testing package | Cognitive-testing protocol, findings, and revisions |
| Representation plan | Target population, sample/mode assessment, recruitment, and limitations |
| Instrument QA | Integrated questionnaire review, test cases, issue log, and approval record |
| Analysis plan | Planned outcomes, subgroups, derived variables, weighting use, tables, and graphics |

## Coauthored LBJ/Univision report · 20%

The class will develop a professional report using the project data. The report should include:

- an executive summary;
- a concise explanation of the research purpose;
- a transparent methods statement;
- substantive findings organized around clear research questions;
- accurate tables and accessible graphics;
- appropriate discussion of uncertainty and limitations; and
- documentation sufficient to reproduce published figures and statistics.

Authorship and branding will depend on the final partnership agreement and documented contributions.

## Individual reflection and contribution statement · 5%

The final reflection identifies the student's contributions, explains one consequential methodological decision, evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of the completed project, and proposes improvements for a future polling cycle.

## Evaluation principles

Work will be evaluated on:

- methodological reasoning;
- accuracy and reproducibility;
- clarity and audience awareness;
- ethical and professional judgment;
- responsiveness to evidence and feedback;
- documentation of decisions; and
- contribution to the collaborative process.

A polished output cannot compensate for an indefensible method, and technical sophistication cannot compensate for unclear communication.
